A concert you watch from inside a VR headset. A performer stands on top of a giant glowing globe, lasers sweep the sky and a ring of fans with phone lights wraps the stage. I explored how scale, light and crowd energy can make a virtual show feel like you are really there.

An AR concept for a Surf Excel campaign. A life-size pack drops into a dusty playground while kids ride their bikes through the dirt around it. I explored how a brand can live inside a real place, so the ad feels like part of the scene rather than something placed on top of it.

ch. 05 · I'm the one holding the pen

a little about me

that's me!

I started in visual communication, learning how things look. Now I study why people do what they do, and design for that.

My projects usually begin away from the screen. I've stood in a vegetable market at three different times of day, surveyed riders about what they can read at a glance, and traced a support chatbot down every dead end. What I find there decides what I draw.

I treat uncertainty as the design problem. When people know what's fresh, what's next or who they're talking to, they relax, and the product gets easier to use.

Off screen you'll find me painting, running, doing yoga, hunting for good coffee and croissants, or saying hello to every dog I pass.

Research
User interviews, field observation, journey mapping, personas, competitive analysis
Design
Information architecture, user flows, wireframes, prototyping, design systems, accessibility
Visual
Typography, editorial and layout design, brand identity, information design
Tools
Figma, Framer, FigJam, Miro, Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects, Procreate

← all workJioCare chatbot

Making SIM porting conversations clear enough to finish.

Redesigning the JioCare chatbot ∙ MyJio

I redesigned the MyJio JioCare chatbot into a structured voice-and-text experience that keeps SIM port conversations clear, continuous and trust-building.

Role
UX research, conversation and interaction design
Timeline
Jan 2025
Type
Redesign concept
Methods
Heuristic evaluation, journey mapping, Double Diamond
Tools
Figma

where it started

JioCare is the support chatbot inside the MyJio app. One of the jobs people bring to it is porting their number to Jio, a task they want to get right the first time.

what was going wrong

Conversations ran into dead ends. Paths were unclear, context was lost between steps and people dropped out before the task was done.

how I worked through it

  1. EvaluateRan a heuristic evaluation of the existing chatbot to find where it broke usability basics.
  2. MapMapped the SIM porting journey to locate pain points, dead ends and drop-offs.
  3. RestructureRedesigned the conversation flows with the Double Diamond process, so every path leads somewhere.
  4. PrototypeBuilt wireframes and high-fidelity prototypes in Figma.

what came out of it

A structured conversation with voice and text input, a clear next step at every turn and AI-assisted support concepts. Together they improve navigation, support clarity and interaction efficiency.

Taking the guesswork out of the daily vegetable run.

The Everyday Vegetable Market ∙ Taaza Otala

I turned field research at Gandhinagar's Sector 21 vegetable market into Taaza Otala, a lightweight digital layer for fresher, calmer buying and smarter vendor stock planning.

Role
Field research, service and UX design
Timeline
Feb 2026
Where
Sector 21 market, Gandhinagar
Methods
Observation, interviews, synthesis
Tools
Figma

where it started

The Sector 21 vegetable market is part of daily life in Gandhinagar. Shoppers and vendors make quick decisions there with very little information to go on.

what was going wrong

Shoppers can't easily tell what's fresh or what a fair price is. Vendors have to guess how much stock to bring. Across every conversation, uncertainty was the real problem.

what I heard

Four themes came up again and again, across two kinds of shoppers.

TimePriceFreshnessStock

how I worked through it

  1. ObserveWatched the market at three different times of day.
  2. ListenInterviewed vendors and customers about freshness, pricing and daily stock.
  3. SynthesiseGrouped the findings into four recurring themes and two shopper types.
  4. DesignPrototyped Taaza Otala as a customer app and a vendor dashboard.

what came out of it

Customers can pre-order, pick a pickup time slot, check reference prices and see freshness information. Vendors get a dashboard that helps them plan how much stock to bring.

← all workTVS Ronin dashboard

A dashboard designed around where the rider is already looking.

TVS Ronin ∙ dashboard redesign

I redesigned the TVS Ronin's digital dashboard around the rider's line of sight, turning survey insights into a centred, high-contrast, ISO-aligned display.

Role
UX research and interface design
Timeline
Nov 2025
Type
Automotive HMI redesign
Methods
Rider survey, ISO guidelines

where it started

The TVS Ronin is a modern-retro motorcycle with a digital dashboard. Riders read it in quick glances while keeping their eyes on the road.

what was going wrong

Information that sits off-centre or lacks contrast takes longer to read, and every extra moment spent looking down is time away from the road.

how I worked through it

  1. SurveyAsked riders what they check on the dashboard and when.
  2. MapMatched the findings to the rider's natural line of sight.
  3. AlignFollowed ISO guidance for vehicle display layout and symbols.
  4. DesignDesigned a centred, high-contrast display.

what came out of it

A centred, high-contrast, ISO-aligned dashboard that puts the most-checked information where the rider is already looking.

A little bit of home for the first months somewhere new.

FromIndia ∙ support from India, wherever you are

I designed FromIndia, a mobile app for Indians living abroad. It puts settling in first, then keeps help from home close when something goes wrong.

Role
Solo UI and UX designer
Timeline
Oct 2026
Duration
2 weeks
Type
Mobile app
Focus
Settling in first
Tools
Figma

where it started

Moving abroad means a long list of firsts: a bank account, a doctor, groceries that taste like home, and people who understand where you came from.

what was going wrong

The answers are scattered across forums, group chats and government sites, and the help people need most is hardest to find when they need it fast.

how I worked through it

  1. ResearchTalked to Indians living abroad about their first months and what they struggled with.
  2. PrioritisePut settling in first and kept SOS and legal help as a secondary flow.
  3. DesignDesigned the app screens in Figma, page by page.
  4. RefineReworked earlier UI screens around what the research showed.

what came out of it

An app that guides people through settling in step by step, with emergency and legal help one tap away when they need it.

Capturing the table's best moments, so nobody has to reach for a phone.

Auto Story Table ∙ human factors in interactive dining

I designed Auto Story Table, a 360° café centrepiece that turns shared moments into ready-to-post stories, with opt-in privacy controls so diners stay present.

Role
Human factors and product concept
Timeline
Mar 2026
Type
Product concept
Focus
Privacy by design

where it started

At cafés, people often pause the moment to film it. Someone holds up a phone, the conversation stops and one person ends up behind the camera instead of at the table.

what was going wrong

How might a table capture the moment for the group, without anyone stepping out of it, and without capturing people who haven't agreed to it?

how it works, step by step

  1. The setupA 360° sensor sits at the centre of the table and sees every angle at once.
  2. The momentAI notices a "hero dish" arriving and records the food and the group together.
  3. The interactionThe system digitally pans to the speaker or the action, with no moving parts.
  4. The processingThe engine picks the best angles and removes fish-eye distortion.
  5. The notificationThe story is compiled and delivered before the bill arrives.
  6. The final exportA multi-perspective story, ready to share, with opt-in privacy controls.

what came out of it

A centrepiece that does the filming so diners can stay present, with privacy controls that keep it opt-in.
